title: Kaalinga Narthanam
body: Krishna was a divine child, born in a beautiful cowherd village called Gokul on the fertile banks of the River Yamuna (North India). He was an incarnation of Lord Vishnu born to rid the world of evil. He was a playful, mischievous boy who played pranks with His friends and stole delicious butter that the village ladies churned out of milk. At the same time, He worked many miracles to vanquish demons that were sent to destroy Him when He was young. The village came to respect, love and worship Him as he grew up to be their saviour.

Kaalinga or Kaliya was a giant five-hooded serpant (Naga) who had wandered down the River Yamuna, straight to Gokul, fearing an enemy (Garuda). His venom was so powerful that for four leagues around him, the water turned bubbling green. Any living thing that touched this water died instantly. Dead fish and algae floated on the water like a warning to anyone who dared come near. Krishna and His friends took the cows out to graze every day. In the afternoon, Krishna would take out His flute and regale everyone with sweet music putting them to sleep. On one such hot day, one of His cows escaped from His gaze and went to the water for a drink. As soon as the cow touched the water, he fell down lifeless. Some of Krishna’s friends went to help the cow and they fell lifeless when they touched the cow.

Krishna heard the cries of His friends and ran down to the river to find them lifeless. He was enraged and jumped in the river to tackle the source – Kaalinga. A bitter battle ensued under water. The entire village assembled to watch in horror. Krishna’s parents clutched their hearts unable to go into the water to save Him. Finally, Kaalinga emerged out of the water beaten black and blue and on top of Kaalinga’s five hoods, Krishna danced playing His flute with one hand while holding Kaalinga’s tail with another hand. This scene reminds us that God always comes to the aid of those who truly believe in Him. I also interpret this story to mean that size doesn’t matter if you have purpose. He takes on an enemy far bigger than Him and emerges successful (granted He is God!).

He danced from one hood to another until Kaanlinga got tired and got ready for the final blow. Kaalinga’s wives beg Him to spare their husband and He relents banishing Kaalinga from the peaceful shores of Yamuna forever. Once Kaalinga leaves, all the dead living beings are raised back to life like a miracle. People sing praise of their savior, Lord Krishna, everyday!
